scope: All source occurrences of lemma 5647 plus selected names, quantities, harm and Sabbath passages.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יַּעֲבִ֧דוּ מִצְרַ֛יִם אֶת ־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּ/פָֽרֶךְ ׃
rows.fluent: The Egyptians worked the Israelites ruthlessly as slaves.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יְמָרְר֨וּ אֶת ־ חַיֵּי/הֶ֜ם בַּ/עֲבֹדָ֣ה קָשָׁ֗ה בְּ/חֹ֨מֶר֙ וּ/בִ/לְבֵנִ֔ים וּ/בְ/כָל ־ עֲבֹדָ֖ה בַּ/שָּׂדֶ֑ה אֵ֚ת כָּל ־ עֲבֹ֣דָתָ֔/ם אֲשֶׁר ־ עָבְד֥וּ בָ/הֶ֖ם בְּ/פָֽרֶךְ ׃
rows.fluent: They made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and brick and every kind of work in the fields. In all their labor, the Egyptians treated them ruthlessly.

rows.hebrew: וַ/תָּבֹ֕אנָה אֶל ־ רְעוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִי/הֶ֑ן וַ/יֹּ֕אמֶר מַדּ֛וּעַ מִהַרְתֶּ֥ן בֹּ֖א הַ/יּֽוֹם ׃
rows.fluent: When they returned to their father Reuel, he asked, “How did you get back so quickly today?”

rows.hebrew: וּ/מֹשֶׁ֗ה הָיָ֥ה רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת ־ צֹ֛אן יִתְר֥וֹ חֹתְנ֖/וֹ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִדְיָ֑ן וַ/יִּנְהַ֤ג אֶת ־ הַ/צֹּאן֙ אַחַ֣ר הַ/מִּדְבָּ֔ר וַ/יָּבֹ֛א אֶל ־ הַ֥ר הָ/אֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽבָ/ה ׃
rows.fluent: Moses was tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כִּֽי ־ אֶֽהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔/ךְ וְ/זֶה ־ לְּ/ךָ֣ הָ/א֔וֹת כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י שְׁלַחְתִּ֑י/ךָ בְּ/הוֹצִֽיאֲ/ךָ֤ אֶת ־ הָ/עָם֙ מִ/מִּצְרַ֔יִם תַּֽעַבְדוּ/ן֙ אֶת ־ הָ֣/אֱלֹהִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָ/הָ֥ר הַ/זֶּֽה ׃
rows.fluent: “I will be with you,” God answered. “This will be the sign that I have sent you: when you bring the people out of Egypt, you all will serve God on this mountain.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֵּ֨לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַ/יָּ֣שָׁב ׀ אֶל ־ יֶ֣תֶר חֹֽתְנ֗/וֹ וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר ל/וֹ֙ אֵ֣לֲכָה נָּ֗א וְ/אָשׁ֨וּבָה֙ אֶל ־ אַחַ֣/י אֲשֶׁר ־ בְּ/מִצְרַ֔יִם וְ/אֶרְאֶ֖ה הַ/עוֹדָ֣/ם חַיִּ֑ים וַ/יֹּ֧אמֶר יִתְר֛וֹ לְ/מֹשֶׁ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְ/שָׁלֽוֹם ׃
rows.fluent: Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said, “Please let me return to my own people in Egypt and see whether they are still alive.” Jethro answered, “Go in peace.”

rows.hebrew: וָ/אֹמַ֣ר אֵלֶ֗י/ךָ שַׁלַּ֤ח אֶת ־ בְּנִ/י֙ וְ/יַֽעַבְדֵ֔/נִי וַ/תְּמָאֵ֖ן לְ/שַׁלְּח֑/וֹ הִנֵּה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י הֹרֵ֔ג אֶת ־ בִּנְ/ךָ֖ בְּכֹרֶֽ/ךָ ׃
rows.fluent: I told you, “Let my son go so that he may serve me,” but you refused to let him go. Now I will kill your son, your firstborn.’”

rows.hebrew: וְ/עַתָּה֙ לְכ֣וּ עִבְד֔וּ וְ/תֶ֖בֶן לֹא ־ יִנָּתֵ֣ן לָ/כֶ֑ם וְ/תֹ֥כֶן לְבֵנִ֖ים תִּתֵּֽנּוּ ׃
rows.fluent: Now go back to work. You will get no straw, but you must deliver the full brick quota.”

rows.hebrew: וְ/גַ֣ם ׀ אֲנִ֣י שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶֽת ־ נַאֲקַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִצְרַ֖יִם מַעֲבִדִ֣ים אֹתָ֑/ם וָ/אֶזְכֹּ֖ר אֶת ־ בְּרִיתִֽ/י ׃
rows.fluent: I myself have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving, and I have remembered my covenant.

rows.hebrew: וְ/אֵ֨לֶּה שְׁמ֤וֹת בְּנֵֽי ־ לֵוִי֙ לְ/תֹ֣לְדֹתָ֔/ם גֵּרְשׁ֕וֹן וּ/קְהָ֖ת וּ/מְרָרִ֑י וּ/שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י לֵוִ֔י שֶׁ֧בַע וּ/שְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּ/מְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: These are the names of Levi’s sons, listed by their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived a hundred and thirty-seven years.

rows.hebrew: וּ/בְנֵ֣י קְהָ֔ת עַמְרָ֣ם וְ/יִצְהָ֔ר וְ/חֶבְר֖וֹן וְ/עֻזִּיאֵ֑ל וּ/שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י קְהָ֔ת שָׁלֹ֧שׁ וּ/שְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּ/מְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Kohath’s sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived a hundred and thirty-three years.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּקַּ֨ח עַמְרָ֜ם אֶת ־ יוֹכֶ֤בֶד דֹּֽדָת/וֹ֙ ל֣/וֹ לְ/אִשָּׁ֔ה וַ/תֵּ֣לֶד ל֔/וֹ אֶֽת ־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְ/אֶת ־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וּ/שְׁנֵי֙ חַיֵּ֣י עַמְרָ֔ם שֶׁ֧בַע וּ/שְׁלֹשִׁ֛ים וּ/מְאַ֖ת שָׁנָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Amram married his aunt Jochebed. She bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived a hundred and thirty-seven years.

rows.hebrew: וּ/מֹשֶׁה֙ בֶּן ־ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְ/אַֽהֲרֹ֔ן בֶּן ־ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ וּ/שְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּ/דַבְּרָ֖/ם אֶל ־ פַּרְעֹֽה ׃ פ
rows.fluent: Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.

rows.hebrew: וְ/אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗י/ו יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָ/עִבְרִים֙ שְׁלָחַ֤/נִי אֵלֶ֨י/ךָ֙ לֵ/אמֹ֔ר שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת ־ עַמִּ֔/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻ֖/נִי בַּ/מִּדְבָּ֑ר וְ/הִנֵּ֥ה לֹא ־ שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ עַד ־ כֹּֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Tell him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you with this message: “Let my people go so they may serve me in the wilderness.” But until now you have not listened.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל ־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל ־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְ/אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗י/ו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת ־ עַמִּ֖/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻֽ/נִי ׃
rows.fluent: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל ־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה הַשְׁכֵּ֤ם בַּ/בֹּ֨קֶר֙ וְ/הִתְיַצֵּב֙ לִ/פְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה הִנֵּ֖ה יוֹצֵ֣א הַ/מָּ֑יְמָ/ה וְ/אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗י/ו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻֽ/נִי ׃
rows.fluent: The LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh as he goes out to the water. Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל ־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל ־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְ/דִבַּרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗י/ו כֹּֽה ־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽ/עִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת ־ עַמִּ֖/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻֽ/נִי ׃
rows.fluent: The LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל ־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם בַּ/בֹּ֔קֶר וְ/הִתְיַצֵּ֖ב לִ/פְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וְ/אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗י/ו כֹּֽה ־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽ/עִבְרִ֔ים שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת ־ עַמִּ֖/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻֽ/נִי ׃
rows.fluent: The LORD said to Moses, “Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh. Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go so they may serve me.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְ/אַהֲרֹן֮ אֶל ־ פַּרְעֹה֒ וַ/יֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗י/ו כֹּֽה ־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽ/עִבְרִ֔ים עַד ־ מָתַ֣י מֵאַ֔נְתָּ לֵ/עָנֹ֖ת מִ/פָּנָ֑/י שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖/י וְ/יַֽעַבְדֻֽ/נִי ׃
rows.fluent: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go so they may serve me.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֹּאמְרוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י פַרְעֹ֜ה אֵלָ֗י/ו עַד ־ מָתַי֙ יִהְיֶ֨ה זֶ֥ה לָ֨/נוּ֙ לְ/מוֹקֵ֔שׁ שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת ־ הָ֣/אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְ/יַֽעַבְד֖וּ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵי/הֶ֑ם הֲ/טֶ֣רֶם תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אָבְדָ֖ה מִצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go to serve the LORD their God. Do you still not realize that Egypt is ruined?”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יּוּשַׁ֞ב אֶת ־ מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְ/אֶֽת ־ אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל ־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַ/יֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵ/הֶ֔ם לְכ֥וּ עִבְד֖וּ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵי/כֶ֑ם מִ֥י וָ/מִ֖י הַ/הֹלְכִֽים ׃
rows.fluent: Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go and serve the LORD your God,” he said. “But exactly who is going?”

rows.hebrew: לֹ֣א כֵ֗ן לְכֽוּ ־ נָ֤א הַ/גְּבָרִים֙ וְ/עִבְד֣וּ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֹתָ֖/הּ אַתֶּ֣ם מְבַקְשִׁ֑ים וַ/יְגָ֣רֶשׁ אֹתָ֔/ם מֵ/אֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה ׃ פ
rows.fluent: No! You men may go and serve the LORD, since that is what you are asking for.” Moses and Aaron were driven out of Pharaoh’s presence.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה אֶל ־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְכוּ֙ עִבְד֣וּ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֔ה רַ֛ק צֹאנְ/כֶ֥ם וּ/בְקַרְ/כֶ֖ם יֻצָּ֑ג גַּֽם ־ טַפְּ/כֶ֖ם יֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמָּ/כֶֽם ׃
rows.fluent: Pharaoh summoned Moses. “Go and serve the LORD,” he said. “Only your flocks and herds must stay behind. Even your little ones may go with you.”

rows.hebrew: וְ/גַם ־ מִקְנֵ֜/נוּ יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗/נוּ לֹ֤א תִשָּׁאֵר֙ פַּרְסָ֔ה כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣/נּוּ נִקַּ֔ח לַ/עֲבֹ֖ד אֶת ־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑י/נוּ וַ/אֲנַ֣חְנוּ לֹֽא ־ נֵדַ֗ע מַֽה ־ נַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֔ה עַד ־ בֹּאֵ֖/נוּ שָֽׁמָּ/ה ׃
rows.fluent: Our livestock must go with us too. Not a hoof will be left behind. We must take from them what we need to serve the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to serve the LORD until we get there.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּקְרָא֩ לְ/מֹשֶׁ֨ה וּֽ/לְ/אַהֲרֹ֜ן לַ֗יְלָה וַ/יֹּ֨אמֶר֙ ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙ מִ/תּ֣וֹךְ עַמִּ֔/י גַּם ־ אַתֶּ֖ם גַּם ־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּ/לְכ֛וּ עִבְד֥וּ אֶת ־ יְהוָ֖ה כְּ/דַבֶּרְ/כֶֽם ׃
rows.fluent: That night he summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “Get up! Leave my people, both you and the Israelites. Go and serve the LORD, as you asked.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּסְע֧וּ בְנֵֽי ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מֵ/רַעְמְסֵ֖ס סֻכֹּ֑תָ/ה כְּ/שֵׁשׁ ־ מֵא֨וֹת אֶ֧לֶף רַגְלִ֛י הַ/גְּבָרִ֖ים לְ/בַ֥ד מִ/טָּֽף ׃
rows.fluent: The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the children.

rows.hebrew: וּ/מוֹשַׁב֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בְּ/מִצְרָ֑יִם שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְ/אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: The Israelites’ stay in Egypt lasted four hundred thirty years.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יְהִ֗י מִ/קֵּץ֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְ/אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַ/יְהִ֗י בְּ/עֶ֨צֶם֙ הַ/יּ֣וֹם הַ/זֶּ֔ה יָֽצְא֛וּ כָּל ־ צִבְא֥וֹת יְהוָ֖ה מֵ/אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: At the end of those four hundred thirty years, on that very day, all the LORD’s divisions left Egypt.

rows.hebrew: וְ/הָיָ֣ה כִֽי ־ יְבִֽיאֲ/ךָ֣ יְהוָ֡ה אֶל ־ אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠/כְּנַעֲנִי וְ/הַ/חִתִּ֨י וְ/הָ/אֱמֹרִ֜י וְ/הַ/חִוִּ֣י וְ/הַ/יְבוּסִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַ/אֲבֹתֶ֨י/ךָ֙ לָ֣/תֶת לָ֔/ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּ/דְבָ֑שׁ וְ/עָבַדְתָּ֛ אֶת ־ הָ/עֲבֹדָ֥ה הַ/זֹּ֖את בַּ/חֹ֥דֶשׁ הַ/זֶּֽה ׃
rows.fluent: When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land flowing with milk and honey that he swore to your ancestors to give you—keep this observance in this month.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יֻּגַּד֙ לְ/מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח הָ/עָ֑ם וַ֠/יֵּהָפֵךְ לְבַ֨ב פַּרְעֹ֤ה וַ/עֲבָדָי/ו֙ אֶל ־ הָ/עָ֔ם וַ/יֹּֽאמרוּ֙ מַה ־ זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֔ינוּ כִּֽי ־ שִׁלַּ֥חְנוּ אֶת ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵ/עָבְדֵֽ/נוּ ׃
rows.fluent: When Egypt’s king was told that the people had fled, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about them. “What have we done?” they said. “We’ve let Israel go and lost their service!”

rows.hebrew: הֲ/לֹא ־ זֶ֣ה הַ/דָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבַּ֨רְנוּ אֵלֶ֤י/ךָ בְ/מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ לֵ/אמֹ֔ר חֲדַ֥ל מִמֶּ֖/נּוּ וְ/נַֽעַבְדָ֣ה אֶת ־ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י ט֥וֹב לָ֨/נוּ֙ עֲבֹ֣ד אֶת ־ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִ/מֻּתֵ֖/נוּ בַּ/מִּדְבָּֽר ׃
rows.fluent: Didn’t we tell you in Egypt, ‘Leave us alone! Let us serve the Egyptians’? It would be better to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness!”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּסְעוּ֙ מֵֽ/אֵילִ֔ם וַ/יָּבֹ֜אוּ כָּל ־ עֲדַ֤ת בְּנֵֽי ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל ־ מִדְבַּר ־ סִ֔ין אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּין ־ אֵילִ֖ם וּ/בֵ֣ין סִינָ֑י בַּ/חֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ לַ/חֹ֣דֶשׁ הַ/שֵּׁנִ֔י לְ/צֵאתָ֖/ם מֵ/אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: They traveled on from Elim, and the whole community of Israelites came to the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai. It was the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.

rows.hebrew: וּ/בְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָֽכְל֤וּ אֶת ־ הַ/מָּן֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה עַד ־ בֹּאָ֖/ם אֶל ־ אֶ֣רֶץ נוֹשָׁ֑בֶת אֶת ־ הַ/מָּן֙ אָֽכְל֔וּ עַד ־ בֹּאָ֕/ם אֶל ־ קְצֵ֖ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן ׃
rows.fluent: The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land. They ate manna until they reached the edge of Canaan.

rows.hebrew: וַ/יִּשְׁמַ֞ע יִתְר֨וֹ כֹהֵ֤ן מִדְיָן֙ חֹתֵ֣ן מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֵת֩ כָּל ־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה אֱלֹהִים֙ לְ/מֹשֶׁ֔ה וּ/לְ/יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַמּ֑/וֹ כִּֽי ־ הוֹצִ֧יא יְהוָ֛ה אֶת ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִ/מִּצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses’ father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and his people Israel—how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.

rows.hebrew: בַּ/חֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ הַ/שְּׁלִישִׁ֔י לְ/צֵ֥את בְּנֵי ־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵ/אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם בַּ/יּ֣וֹם הַ/זֶּ֔ה בָּ֖אוּ מִדְבַּ֥ר סִינָֽי ׃
rows.fluent: In the third month after the Israelites left Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.

rows.hebrew: לֹֽא ־ תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה לָ/הֶ֖ם וְ/לֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑/ם כִּ֣י אָֽנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨י/ךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָבֹ֧ת עַל ־ בָּנִ֛ים עַל ־ שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְ/עַל ־ רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְ/שֹׂנְאָֽ/י ׃
rows.fluent: Do not bow down to them or serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, bringing the fathers’ guilt upon their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me,

rows.hebrew: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּֽעֲבֹ֔ד וְ/עָשִׂ֖יתָ כָּל ־ מְלַאכְתֶּֽ/ךָ ׃
rows.fluent: Work for six days and do all your labor,

rows.hebrew: כִּ֤י תִקְנֶה֙ עֶ֣בֶד עִבְרִ֔י שֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים יַעֲבֹ֑ד וּ/בַ֨/שְּׁבִעִ֔ת יֵצֵ֥א לַֽ/חָפְשִׁ֖י חִנָּֽם ׃
rows.fluent: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years. In the seventh year he is to go free, without payment.

rows.hebrew: וְ/הִגִּישׁ֤/וֹ אֲדֹנָי/ו֙ אֶל ־ הָ֣/אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְ/הִגִּישׁ/וֹ֙ אֶל ־ הַ/דֶּ֔לֶת א֖וֹ אֶל ־ הַ/מְּזוּזָ֑ה וְ/רָצַ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤י/ו אֶת ־ אָזְנ/וֹ֙ בַּ/מַּרְצֵ֔עַ וַ/עֲבָד֖/וֹ לְ/עֹלָֽם ׃ ס
rows.fluent: his master is to bring him before God and then bring him to the door or the doorpost. His master is to pierce his ear with an awl, and he will serve him permanently.

rows.hebrew: וְ/כִֽי ־ יִמְכֹּ֥ר אִ֛ישׁ אֶת ־ בִּתּ֖/וֹ לְ/אָמָ֑ה לֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א כְּ/צֵ֥את הָ/עֲבָדִֽים ׃
rows.fluent: If a man sells his daughter as a slave, she is not to leave as male slaves do.

rows.hebrew: אִם ־ רָעָ֞ה בְּ/עֵינֵ֧י אֲדֹנֶ֛י/הָ אֲשֶׁר ־ לא יְעָדָ֖/הּ וְ/הֶפְדָּ֑/הּ לְ/עַ֥ם נָכְרִ֛י לֹא ־ יִמְשֹׁ֥ל לְ/מָכְרָ֖/הּ בְּ/בִגְד/וֹ ־ בָֽ/הּ ׃
rows.fluent: If she displeases the master who designated her for himself, he must allow her to be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, because he has betrayed her.
If he designates her for his son, he must treat her according to the rights of daughters.

rows.hebrew: אִם ־ אַחֶ֖רֶת יִֽקַּֽח ־ ל֑/וֹ שְׁאֵרָ֛/הּ כְּסוּתָ֥/הּ וְ/עֹנָתָ֖/הּ לֹ֥א יִגְרָֽע ׃
rows.fluent: If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the first woman’s food, clothing, or marital rights.

rows.hebrew: וְ/אִם ־ שְׁלָ֨שׁ ־ אֵ֔לֶּה לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה לָ֑/הּ וְ/יָצְאָ֥ה חִנָּ֖ם אֵ֥ין כָּֽסֶף ׃ ס
rows.fluent: If he does not provide these three things for her, she is to leave without payment, owing no money.

rows.hebrew: וְ/כִֽי ־ יַכֶּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶת ־ עַבְדּ֜/וֹ א֤וֹ אֶת ־ אֲמָת/וֹ֙ בַּ/שֵּׁ֔בֶט וּ/מֵ֖ת תַּ֣חַת יָד֑/וֹ נָקֹ֖ם יִנָּקֵֽם ׃
rows.fluent: If a man beats his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies under his hand, that death must be avenged.

rows.hebrew: אַ֥ךְ אִם ־ י֛וֹם א֥וֹ יוֹמַ֖יִם יַעֲמֹ֑ד לֹ֣א יֻקַּ֔ם כִּ֥י כַסְפּ֖/וֹ הֽוּא ׃ ס
rows.fluent: But if the slave survives a day or two, no vengeance is to be taken, because the slave is his money.

rows.hebrew: וְ/כִֽי ־ יַכֶּ֨ה אִ֜ישׁ אֶת ־ עֵ֥ין עַבְדּ֛/וֹ אֽוֹ ־ אֶת ־ עֵ֥ין אֲמָת֖/וֹ וְ/שִֽׁחֲתָ֑/הּ לַֽ/חָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖/נּוּ תַּ֥חַת עֵינֽ/וֹ ׃ ס
rows.fluent: If a man strikes and destroys the eye of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free in compensation for the eye.

rows.hebrew: וְ/אִם ־ שֵׁ֥ן עַבְדּ֛/וֹ אֽוֹ ־ שֵׁ֥ן אֲמָת֖/וֹ יַפִּ֑יל לַֽ/חָפְשִׁ֥י יְשַׁלְּחֶ֖/נּוּ תַּ֥חַת שִׁנּֽ/וֹ ׃ פ
rows.fluent: If he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free in compensation for the tooth.

rows.hebrew: וְ/גֵ֥ר לֹא ־ תוֹנֶ֖ה וְ/לֹ֣א תִלְחָצֶ֑/נּוּ כִּֽי ־ גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּ/אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: Do not wrong or oppress a foreigner living among you, because you were foreigners in Egypt.

rows.hebrew: כָּל ־ אַלְמָנָ֥ה וְ/יָת֖וֹם לֹ֥א תְעַנּֽוּ/ן ׃
rows.fluent: Do not mistreat any widow or fatherless child.

rows.hebrew: אִם ־ עַנֵּ֥ה תְעַנֶּ֖ה אֹת֑/וֹ כִּ֣י אִם ־ צָעֹ֤ק יִצְעַק֙ אֵלַ֔/י שָׁמֹ֥עַ אֶשְׁמַ֖ע צַעֲקָתֽ/וֹ ׃
rows.fluent: If you do mistreat them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.

rows.hebrew: וְ/חָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔/י וְ/הָרַגְתִּ֥י אֶתְ/כֶ֖ם בֶּ/חָ֑רֶב וְ/הָי֤וּ נְשֵׁי/כֶם֙ אַלְמָנ֔וֹת וּ/בְנֵי/כֶ֖ם יְתֹמִֽים ׃ פ
rows.fluent: My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.

rows.hebrew: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְ/ךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖/וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖/נּוּ לֽ/וֹ ׃ ס
rows.fluent: If you come across your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering away, be sure to take it back to him.

rows.hebrew: כִּֽי ־ תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲ/ךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔/וֹ וְ/חָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵ/עֲזֹ֣ב ל֑/וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽ/וֹ ׃ ס
rows.fluent: If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying under its load, do not leave him without help. Be sure to help him with it.

rows.hebrew: וְ/גֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְ/אַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת ־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַ/גֵּ֔ר כִּֽי ־ גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּ/אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם ׃
rows.fluent: Do not oppress a foreigner living among you. You yourselves know what it is like to be a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.

rows.hebrew: לֹֽא ־ תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵ/אלֹֽהֵי/הֶם֙ וְ/לֹ֣א תָֽעָבְדֵ֔/ם וְ/לֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּ/מַֽעֲשֵׂי/הֶ֑ם כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔/ם וְ/שַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵי/הֶֽם ׃
rows.fluent: Do not bow down to their gods, serve them, or imitate their practices. You must tear them down completely and smash their sacred pillars.

rows.hebrew: וַ/עֲבַדְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵי/כֶ֔ם וּ/בֵרַ֥ךְ אֶֽת ־ לַחְמְ/ךָ֖ וְ/אֶת ־ מֵימֶ֑י/ךָ וַ/הֲסִרֹתִ֥י מַחֲלָ֖ה מִ/קִּרְבֶּֽ/ךָ ׃
rows.fluent: Serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and water. I will remove sickness from among you.

rows.hebrew: לֹ֤א יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּ/אַרְצְ/ךָ֔ פֶּן ־ יַחֲטִ֥יאוּ אֹתְ/ךָ֖ לִ֑/י כִּ֤י תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת ־ אֱלֹ֣הֵי/הֶ֔ם כִּֽי ־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְ/ךָ֖ לְ/מוֹקֵֽשׁ ׃ פ
rows.fluent: They must not live in your land, or they will lead you to sin against me. If you serve their gods, it will become a snare for you.”

rows.hebrew: וַ/יָּבֹ֥א מֹשֶׁ֛ה בְּ/ת֥וֹךְ הֶ/עָנָ֖ן וַ/יַּ֣עַל אֶל ־ הָ/הָ֑ר וַ/יְהִ֤י מֹשֶׁה֙ בָּ/הָ֔ר אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְ/אַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה ׃ פ
rows.fluent: Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. He stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עָשׂ֥וּ אֲר֖וֹן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֨יִם וָ/חֵ֜צִי אָרְכּ֗/וֹ וְ/אַמָּ֤ה וָ/חֵ֨צִי֙ רָחְבּ֔/וֹ וְ/אַמָּ֥ה וָ/חֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽ/וֹ ׃
rows.fluent: Have them make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עָשִׂ֥יתָ כַפֹּ֖רֶת זָהָ֣ב טָה֑וֹר אַמָּתַ֤יִם וָ/חֵ֨צִי֙ אָרְכָּ֔/הּ וְ/אַמָּ֥ה וָ/חֵ֖צִי רָחְבָּֽ/הּ ׃
rows.fluent: Make an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עָשִׂ֥יתָ שֻׁלְחָ֖ן עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים אַמָּתַ֤יִם אָרְכּ/וֹ֙ וְ/אַמָּ֣ה רָחְבּ֔/וֹ וְ/אַמָּ֥ה וָ/חֵ֖צִי קֹמָתֽ/וֹ ׃
rows.fluent: Make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

rows.hebrew: כִּכָּ֛ר זָהָ֥ב טָה֖וֹר יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֹתָ֑/הּ אֵ֥ת כָּל ־ הַ/כֵּלִ֖ים הָ/אֵֽלֶּה ׃
rows.fluent: Use one talent of pure gold to make it and all these utensils.

rows.hebrew: אֹ֣רֶךְ ׀ הַ/יְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽ/אַחַ֗ת שְׁמֹנֶ֤ה וְ/עֶשְׂרִים֙ בָּֽ/אַמָּ֔ה וְ/רֹ֨חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּ/אַמָּ֔ה הַ/יְרִיעָ֖ה הָ/אֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לְ/כָל ־ הַ/יְרִיעֹֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains must have the same dimensions.

rows.hebrew: אֹ֣רֶךְ ׀ הַ/יְרִיעָ֣ה הָֽ/אַחַ֗ת שְׁלֹשִׁים֙ בָּֽ/אַמָּ֔ה וְ/רֹ֨חַב֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע בָּ/אַמָּ֔ה הַ/יְרִיעָ֖ה הָ/אֶחָ֑ת מִדָּ֣ה אַחַ֔ת לְ/עַשְׁתֵּ֥י עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה יְרִיעֹֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven must have the same dimensions.

rows.hebrew: עֶ֥שֶׂר אַמּ֖וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַ/קָּ֑רֶשׁ וְ/אַמָּה֙ וַ/חֲצִ֣י הָֽ/אַמָּ֔ה רֹ֖חַב הַ/קֶּ֥רֶשׁ הָ/אֶחָֽד ׃
rows.fluent: Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עָשִׂ֥יתָ אֶת ־ הַ/מִּזְבֵּ֖חַ עֲצֵ֣י שִׁטִּ֑ים חָמֵשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת אֹ֜רֶךְ וְ/חָמֵ֧שׁ אַמּ֣וֹת רֹ֗חַב רָב֤וּעַ יִהְיֶה֙ הַ/מִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְ/שָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת קֹמָתֽ/וֹ ׃
rows.fluent: “Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, forming a square, and three cubits high.

rows.hebrew: וְ/עָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֖ת חֲצַ֣ר הַ/מִּשְׁכָּ֑ן לִ/פְאַ֣ת נֶֽגֶב ־ תֵּ֠ימָנָ/ה קְלָעִ֨ים לֶ/חָצֵ֜ר שֵׁ֣שׁ מָשְׁזָ֗ר מֵאָ֤ה בָֽ/אַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ לַ/פֵּאָ֖ה הָ/אֶחָֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Make a courtyard for the tabernacle. Along its south side, put hangings of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long for that side,

rows.hebrew: וְ/רֹ֤חַב הֶֽ/חָצֵר֙ לִ/פְאַת ־ יָ֔ם קְלָעִ֖ים חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה עַמֻּדֵי/הֶ֣ם עֲשָׂרָ֔ה וְ/אַדְנֵי/הֶ֖ם עֲשָׂרָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Across the west end of the courtyard, put hangings fifty cubits wide, with ten pillars and ten bases.

rows.hebrew: וּ/לְ/שַׁ֨עַר הֶֽ/חָצֵ֜ר מָסָ֣ךְ ׀ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה תְּכֵ֨לֶת וְ/אַרְגָּמָ֜ן וְ/תוֹלַ֧עַת שָׁנִ֛י וְ/שֵׁ֥שׁ מָשְׁזָ֖ר מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה רֹקֵ֑ם עַמֻּֽדֵי/הֶם֙ אַרְבָּעָ֔ה וְ/אַדְנֵי/הֶ֖ם אַרְבָּעָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: For the courtyard entrance, make a screen twenty cubits wide, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, worked in embroidery, with four pillars and four bases.

rows.hebrew: אַמָּ֨ה אָרְכּ֜/וֹ וְ/אַמָּ֤ה רָחְבּ/וֹ֙ רָב֣וּעַ יִהְיֶ֔ה וְ/אַמָּתַ֖יִם קֹמָת֑/וֹ מִמֶּ֖/נּוּ קַרְנֹתָֽי/ו ׃
rows.fluent: It is to be a cubit long and a cubit wide, forming a square, and two cubits high. Its horns must be of one piece with it.

rows.hebrew: זֶ֣ה ׀ יִתְּנ֗וּ כָּל ־ הָ/עֹבֵר֙ עַל ־ הַ/פְּקֻדִ֔ים מַחֲצִ֥ית הַ/שֶּׁ֖קֶל בְּ/שֶׁ֣קֶל הַ/קֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֤ים גֵּרָה֙ הַ/שֶּׁ֔קֶל מַחֲצִ֣ית הַ/שֶּׁ֔קֶל תְּרוּמָ֖ה לַֽ/יהוָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Everyone passing into the count must give half a shekel by the sanctuary standard—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as a contribution to the LORD.

rows.hebrew: כֹּ֗ל הָ/עֹבֵר֙ עַל ־ הַ/פְּקֻדִ֔ים מִ/בֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָ/מָ֑עְלָ/ה יִתֵּ֖ן תְּרוּמַ֥ת יְהוָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: Everyone counted who is twenty years old or older must give the LORD’s contribution.

rows.hebrew: רְאֵ֖ה קָרָ֣אתִֽי בְ/שֵׁ֑ם בְּצַלְאֵ֛ל בֶּן ־ אוּרִ֥י בֶן ־ ח֖וּר לְ/מַטֵּ֥ה יְהוּדָֽה ׃
rows.fluent: “Look, I have called Bezalel by name, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

rows.hebrew: וַ/אֲנִ֞י הִנֵּ֧ה נָתַ֣תִּי אִתּ֗/וֹ אֵ֣ת אָהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן ־ אֲחִֽיסָמָךְ֙ לְ/מַטֵּה ־ דָ֔ן וּ/בְ/לֵ֥ב כָּל ־ חֲכַם ־ לֵ֖ב נָתַ֣תִּי חָכְמָ֑ה וְ/עָשׂ֕וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל ־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִֽ/ךָ ׃
rows.fluent: I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to work with him. I have given wisdom to every skilled worker, so they can make everything I commanded you:

rows.hebrew: שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִים֮ יֵעָשֶׂ֣ה מְלָאכָה֒ וּ/בַ/יּ֣וֹם הַ/שְּׁבִיעִ֗י שַׁבַּ֧ת שַׁבָּת֛וֹן קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַ/יהוָ֑ה כָּל ־ הָ/עֹשֶׂ֧ה מְלָאכָ֛ה בְּ/י֥וֹם הַ/שַּׁבָּ֖ת מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Work may be done for six days, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who works on the Sabbath day must be put to death.

rows.hebrew: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲבֹ֔ד וּ/בַ/יּ֥וֹם הַ/שְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת בֶּ/חָרִ֥ישׁ וּ/בַ/קָּצִ֖יר תִּשְׁבֹּֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Work for six days, but stop on the seventh. Even during plowing and harvest, you must stop.

rows.hebrew: שֵׁ֣שֶׁת יָמִים֮ תֵּעָשֶׂ֣ה מְלָאכָה֒ וּ/בַ/יּ֣וֹם הַ/שְּׁבִיעִ֗י יִהְיֶ֨ה לָ/כֶ֥ם קֹ֛דֶשׁ שַׁבַּ֥ת שַׁבָּת֖וֹן לַ/יהוָ֑ה כָּל ־ הָ/עֹשֶׂ֥ה ב֛/וֹ מְלָאכָ֖ה יוּמָֽת ׃
rows.fluent: Work may be done for six days, but the seventh must be holy to you, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Anyone who works on it must be put to death.

rows.hebrew: אֵ֣לֶּה פְקוּדֵ֤י הַ/מִּשְׁכָּן֙ מִשְׁכַּ֣ן הָ/עֵדֻ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר פֻּקַּ֖ד עַל ־ פִּ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה עֲבֹדַת֙ הַ/לְוִיִּ֔ם בְּ/יַד֙ אִֽיתָמָ֔ר בֶּֽן ־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן הַ/כֹּהֵֽן ׃
rows.fluent: This is the account of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, recorded at Moses’ command. The Levites carried out the work under Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

rows.hebrew: וּ/בְצַלְאֵ֛ל בֶּן ־ אוּרִ֥י בֶן ־ ח֖וּר לְ/מַטֵּ֣ה יְהוּדָ֑ה עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֛ת כָּל ־ אֲשֶׁר ־ צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת ־ מֹשֶֽׁה ׃
rows.fluent: Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD had commanded Moses.

rows.hebrew: וְ/אִתּ֗/וֹ אָהֳלִיאָ֞ב בֶּן ־ אֲחִיסָמָ֛ךְ לְ/מַטֵּה ־ דָ֖ן חָרָ֣שׁ וְ/חֹשֵׁ֑ב וְ/רֹקֵ֗ם בַּ/תְּכֵ֨לֶת֙ וּ/בָֽ/אַרְגָּמָ֔ן וּ/בְ/תוֹלַ֥עַת הַ/שָּׁנִ֖י וּ/בַ/שֵּֽׁשׁ ׃ ס
rows.fluent: With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, an engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
